text:
Columbus had a two-goal lead after one period and then watched it dissolve. Kent Johnson's wrist shot with 12 seconds left in the first made it 2-0, but it was a 6 percent chance, the kind of goal that flatters a team. Over the next two periods St. Louis outchanced the Blue Jackets 3.12 to 0.82 in expected goals, and the 5-3 final at Enterprise Center matched how the game was actually played.

The turn came in the second. Jake Neighbours cut it to 2-1 with a slap shot at 6:10, Jimmy Snuggerud deflected in the tying goal less than three minutes later, and he beat Jet Greaves again at 12:32 for a 3-2 lead. Dylan Holloway assisted on all three of those goals and finished with three assists, while Robert Thomas, who set up the third, drove 2.23 expected goals for St. Louis during his shifts against 0.68 for Columbus. The Blues finished with 58 shot attempts to 48 and, by the simulation of every shot, deserved to win 74 percent of the time.

Cole Sillinger tied it at 3-3 early in the third, but the pressure never eased. Jonatan Berggren put St. Louis back in front at 9:33, and Pavel Buchnevich added an unassisted goal with 43 seconds left. Greaves was a little below expected over the game, but he faced 3.14 expected goals and gave up four. Jordan Binnington allowed three on 1.77 expected, so Columbus got its goals, just not enough sustained pressure to hold the lead.
